content: Erythromycin stearate interacts with various drugs and substances, primarily by affecting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism or the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, altered therapeutic effects, or heightened toxicity. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions: 1. Erythromycin stearate and quinupristin/dalfopristin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases erythromycin levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QTc interval prolongation. 2. Erythromycin stearate and ranolazine: Erythromycin increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Erythromycin stearate and repaglinide: Erythromycin raises repaglinide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative. 4. Erythromycin stearate and repotrectinib: Erythromycin increases repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 5. Erythromycin stearate and resmetirom: Erythromycin raises resmetirom levels through OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 6. Erythromycin stearate and revefenacin: Erythromycin increases revefenacin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Avoid coadministration. 7. Erythromycin stearate and ribociclib: Ribociclib increases erythromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 8. Erythromycin stearate and rifabutin: Erythromycin increases rifabutin levels by reducing its metabolism, while rifabutin decreases erythromycin levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 9. Erythromycin stearate and rifampin/rifapentine: Both drugs reduce erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 10. Erythromycin stearate and rimegepant: Erythromycin increases rimegepant levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 11. Erythromycin stearate and riociguat: Erythromycin raises riociguat levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 12. Erythromycin stearate and ritonavir: Both drugs increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Erythromycin stearate and romidepsin: Erythromycin increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 14. Erythromycin stearate and rufinamide: Rufinamide decreases erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 15. Erythromycin stearate and selumetinib: Erythromycin increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin stearate and sertraline/sevoflurane: Both combinations increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 17. Erythromycin stearate and silodosin: Erythromycin raises silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 18. Erythromycin stearate and siponimod: Erythromycin increases siponimod levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 19. Erythromycin stearate and sirolimus: Erythromycin raises sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 20. Erythromycin stearate and solifenacin: Erythromycin increases solifenacin levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 21. Erythromycin stearate and sotarasib: Sotarasib reduces erythromycin levels via P-glycoprotein induction. Avoid coadministration or adjust the dose as needed. 22. Erythromycin stearate and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 23. Erythromycin stearate and sulbactam/durlobactam: Erythromycin increases sulbactam levels by inhibiting OATP1 transport. Avoid coadministration. 24. Erythromycin stearate and sunitinib: Erythromycin raises sunitinib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative. 25.
